item.title: Amazon Bedrock Adds Structured Output Support for Anthropic Claude Models
item.description:
Amazon Bedrock Adds Structured Output Support for Anthropic Claude Models

Amazon Bedrock now supports structured outputs for all Anthropic Claude models, enabling developers to receive schema-compliant JSON responses across both bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints.

🧩 How it works

Structured outputs use constrained decoding to enforce JSON schemas during token generation. This process shifts output formatting from probabilistic to deterministic, ensuring the model does not produce tokens that violate the defined schema.

Key mechanisms include:

Mechanism Function Use Case
JSON Schema output format Control response structure Data extraction, report generation, API responses
Strict tool use Validate tool parameters Agentic workflows, function calling, multi-step automation

⚙️ Key details

  • Compliance: Amazon Bedrock validates JSON schemas against the JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 subset.
  • Performance: The system compiles a grammar artifact for new schemas. These are cached for 24 hours per account to improve subsequent request speeds.
  • Efficiency: By constraining responses to only defined fields, output token counts are reduced, which can lower inference costs for high-volume workloads.
  • Implementation: On the bedrock-runtime endpoint, the schema is placed in output_config.format as a JSON object.
  • Tooling: On the bedrock-mantle endpoint, setting strict: true constrains tool inputs to match the provided schema exactly.

🚀 Availability

  • Endpoints: Supported on both bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle.
  • Inference: Works with batch inference for asynchronous processing.
  • Cross-Region: Supported on the bedrock-runtime endpoint for cross-Region inference without additional setup.
  • Real-time: Structured responses can be streamed as typed events.

💡 Why it matters

Structured outputs eliminate common issues such as JSON.parse() errors and parsing exceptions. Because responses are type-safe and required fields are guaranteed to be present, developers can build more reliable agentic workflows that interact with server-side tools.

#AmazonBedrock #AnthropicClaude #JSON #GenerativeAI #API

Source: Structured outputs for Anthropic Claude models on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Codex Pooler Introduced as Self-Hosted Gateway for Codex-Compatible Agents
item.description:
Codex Pooler Introduced as Self-Hosted Gateway for Codex-Compatible Agents

Codex Pooler is a self-hosted gateway designed to run Codex-compatible agents, tools, and automation using stable Pool API keys.

🔍 Overview

Codex Pooler allows operators to manage pools, accounts, API keys, saved resets, routing, request accounting, audit logs, and health. The system is designed so that operators do not store raw Codex secrets, bearer tokens, prompts, files, audio, or images.

🧩 How it works

Clients send OpenAI-compatible or Codex backend requests to the Codex Pooler. The system then selects an eligible account based on the following criteria:

  • Model support
  • Quota evidence
  • Limits
  • Session continuity
  • Routing policy
  • Health

⚙️ Key details

Feature Description
Stable Pool API keys Provides clients with one credential regardless of whether the Pool has one or several upstream accounts, avoiding the distribution of raw Codex account material.
Eligibility-aware routing Routes requests to accounts with matching health, session state, Pool policy, usable quota evidence, and compatible model support.
Codex backend compatibility Allows Codex-compatible clients to point at Codex Pooler while maintaining usage, compacting, and responses.

💡 Why it matters

  • Credential Isolation: It works with one upstream Codex account for client normalization, metadata-only operations, saved reset visibility, and credential isolation.
  • Scalability: Additional accounts can be added for routing and shared capacity across eligible accounts.
  • Stability: The Pool key remains stable even when capacity, reset policy, lifecycle state, and upstream assignments change.
  • Administrative Control: Instance owners maintain the global administration surface, while instance admins are restricted to their assigned Pools.

#Codex #API #AIagents #SelfHosted

Source: icoretech/codex-pooler

item.title: OpenRouter Model Routing and Provider Control Features
item.description:
OpenRouter Model Routing and Provider Control Features

OpenRouter provides an API endpoint that automatically handles fallbacks and selects the most cost-effective option for model requests.

⚙️ Key details

Because different providers use various serving software, optimizations, and settings, the same OpenRouter endpoint can result in requests that behave in different ways. These differences include:

  • Some providers lack vision capability for vision models.
  • The processing of the reasoning effort option can differ between providers.

🧩 How it works

Users have tools to manage how their requests are routed:

  • provider.only option: Allows users to control which specific provider is routed to.
  • /endpoints method: Returns a list of available providers for a specific model ID.

#OpenRouter #API #LLM #ModelRouting

Source: So you want to use OpenRouter?

item.title: OpenAI introduces ChatGPT Images 2.5
item.description:
OpenAI introduces ChatGPT Images 2.5

OpenAI has released ChatGPT Images 2.5, an update to image generation models that have been used for more than 3 billion images across ChatGPT Images and the GPT‑Image models in the API.

⚙️ Key details

This latest release includes several improvements:

  • Faster response times
  • Better ability to preserve subjects in reference photos
  • Improved instruction-following ability across multiple turns

🚀 Availability

Two new model IDs are available in the API:

Model ID Use Case
gpt-image-2.5-sunburst Workflows where editing precision matters most
gpt-image-2.5-flare Fast, high-quality everyday image generation

#OpenAI #ChatGPT #ImageGeneration #API

Source: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5
